passages.english: Linguistically, the word "Arab" means deserts and waste barren land well-nigh waterless and treeless. Ever since the dawn of history, the Arabian Peninsula and its people have been called as such.

passages.english: The Arabian Peninsula is enclosed in the west by the Red Sea and Sinai, in the east by the Arabian Gulf, in the south by the Arabian Sea, which is an extension of the Indian Ocean, and in the north by old Syria and part of Iraq. The area is estimated between a million and a million and a quarter square miles.

passages.english: Thanks to its geographical position, the peninsula has always maintained great importance.. Considering its internal setting, it is mostly deserts and sandy places, which has rendered it inaccessible to foreigners and invaders, and allowed its people complete liberty and independence through the ages, despite the presence of two neighbouring great empires.

passages.english: Its external setting, on the other hand, caused it to be the centre of the old world and provided it with sea and land links with most nations at the time. Thanks to this strategic position the Arabian Peninsula had become the centre for trade, culture, religion and art.

passages.sourceEnglish: Arab kinfolks have been divided according to lineage into three groups:

passages.english: 1. Perishing Arabs: The ancient Arabs, of whose history little is known, and of whom were ‘Ad, Thamud , Tasam, Jadis, Emlaq, and others. 2. Pure Arabs: Who originated from the progeny of Ya‘rub bin Yashjub bin Qahtan. They were also called Qahtanian Arabs. 3. Arabized Arabs: Who originated from the progeny of Ishmael. They were also called ‘Adnanian Arabs.

passages.english: Jafna bin ‘Amr and his family, headed for Syria where he settled and initiated the kingdom of Ghassan who was so named after a spring of water, in Hijaz, where they stopped on their way to Syria. 2. Lakhm and Judham: Of whom was Nasr bin Rabi‘a, father of Manadhira, Kings of Heerah. 3. Banu Tai’: Who also emigrated northwards to settle by the so- called Aja and Salma Mountains which were consequently named as Tai’ Mountains. 4. Kinda: Who dwelt in Bahrain but were expelled to Hadramout and Najd where they instituted a powerful government but not for long , for the whole tribe soon faded away.

passages.english: It is known that Abraham (peace be upon him) left Ar for Harran and then for Palestine, which he made headquarters for his Message. He wandered all over the area. When he went to Egypt, the Pharaoh tried to do evil to his wife Sarah, but Allah saved her and the Pharaoh’s wicked scheme recoiled on him. He thus came to realize her strong attachment to Allah , and, in acknowledgment of her grace, the Pharaoh rendered his daughter Hagar at Sarah’s service, but Sarah gave Hagar to Abraham as a wife. [Bukhari 1/474]

passages.english: Abraham returned to Palestine where Hagar gave birth to Ishmael. Sarah became so jealous of Hagar that she forced Abraham to send Hagar and her baby away to a plantless valley on a small hill in Hijaz, by the Sacred House, exposed to the wearing of floods coming right and left. He chose for them a place under a lofty tree above Zamzam near the upper side of the Mosque in Makkah where neither people nor water was available, and went back to Palestine leaving with his wife and baby a leather case with some dates and a pot of water. Not before long, they ran out of both food and water, but thanks to Allah ’s favour water gushed forth to sustain them for sometime. The whole story of Zamzam spring is already known to everybody. [Bukhari 1/475]

passages.english: When Ishmael became a young man, he learned Arabic at the hand of the tribe of Jurhum, who loved him with great admiration and gave him one of their women as a wife, soon after his mother died. Having wanted to see his wife and son again, Abraham came to Makkah, after Ishmael’s marriage, but he didn’t find him at home. He asked Ishmael’s wife about her husband and how they were doing. She complained of poverty, so he asked her to tell Ishmael to change his doorstep. Ishmael understood the message, divorced his wife and got married to the daughter of Mudad bin ‘Amr, chief of the tribe of Jurhum. [Qalb Jazeerat Al-Arab, p 230]

passages.sourceEnglish: When Ishmael became a young man, he learned Arabic at the hand of the tribe of Jurhum, who loved him with great admiration and gave him one of their women as a wife, soon after his mother died. Having wanted to see his wife and son again, Abraham came to Makkah, after Ishmael’s marriage, but he didn’t find him at home. He asked Ishmael’s wife about her husband and how they were doing. She complained of poverty, so he asked her to tell Ishmael to change his doorstep. passages.english: A third time, Abraham came to Makkah to find Ishmael sharpening an arrow under a lofty tree near Zamzam. The meeting, after a very long journey of separation, was very touching for a father so affectionate and a so dutiful and righteous son. This time, father and son built Al-Ka‘bah and raised its pillars, and Abraham, in compliance with Allah ’s Commandment, called unto people to make pilgrimage to it.

passages.english: By the grace of Allah , Ishmael had twelve sons from the daughter of Mudad, whose names were Nabet, Qidar, Edbael, Mebsham, Mishma’, Duma, Micha, Hudud, Yetma, Yetour, Nafis and Qidman, and who ultimately formed twelve tribes inhabiting Makkah and trading between Yemen, geographical Syria and Egypt. Later on, these tribes spread all over, and even outside, the peninsula. All their tidings went into oblivion except for the descendants of Nabet and Qidar.

passages.english: The Nabeteans – sons of Nabet – established a flourishing civilization in the north of Hijaz, they instituted a powerful government which spread out its domain over all neighbouring tribes, and made Petra their capital. Nobody dared challenge their authority until the Romans came and managed to eliminate their kingdom. After extensive research and painstaking investigation, Mr. Sulaiman An-Nadwi came to the conclusion that the Ghassanide kings, along with the Aws and Khazraj were not likely to be Qahtanians but rather Nabeteans. [Tareekh Ard Al-Qur'an 2/78-86]

passages.english: Descendants of Qidar, the son of Ishmael, lived long in Makkah increasing in number, of them issued ‘Adnan and son Ma‘ad, to whom ‘Adnanian Arabs traced back their ancestry. ‘Adnan is the twenty-first grandfather in the series of the Prophetic ancestry. It was said that whenever Prophet Muhammad ﷺ spoke of his ancestry he would stop at ‘Adnan and say: "Genealogists tell lies" and did not go farther than him. A group of scholars, however, favoured the probability of going beyond ‘Adnan attaching no significance to the aforementioned Prophetic Hadith. They went on to say that there were exactly forty fathers between ‘Adnan and Abraham (peace be upon him). [Rahmat-ul-lil'alameen 2/7-17]

passages.english: Nizar, Ma‘ad’s only son , had four sons who branched out into four great tribes; Eyad, Anmar, Rabi‘a and Mudar. These last two sub-branched into several septs. Rabi‘a fathered Asad, ‘Anazah, ‘Abdul Qais, and Wa’il’s two sons (Bakr and Taghlib), Hanifa and many others.

passages.english: Mudar tribes branched out into two great divisions: Qais ‘Ailan bin Mudar and septs of Elias bin Mudar. Of Qais ‘Ailan were the Banu Saleem, Banu Hawazin, and Banu Ghatafan of whom descended ‘Abs, Zubyan, Ashja‘ and Ghani bin A‘sur. Of Elias bin Mudar were Tamim bin Murra, Hudhail bin Mudrika, Banu Asad bin Khuzaimah and septs of Kinana bin Khuzaimah, of whom came Quraish, the descendants of Fahr bin Malik bin An-Nadr bin Kinana.

passages.sourceEnglish: Prophet Muhammad [pbuh] said:

passages.english: "Allah selected Ishmael from the sons of Abraham, Kinana from the sons of Ishmael, Quraish from the sons of Kinana, Hashim from the sons of Quraish and He selected me from the sons of Hashim." [Muslim 2/245; Tirmidhi 2/201]

sourceBlocks.text: "All? selected Ishmael from the sons of Abraham, Kinana from the sons of Ishmael, Quraish from the sons of Kinana, Hashim from the sons of Quraish and He selected me from the sons of Hashim." [Muslim 2/245; Tirmidhi 2/201]

passages.kashmiri: «اللہ تعالہَن چُھن ابراہیم سٕندٮ۪ن نِچوَن منٛزٕ اسماعیل، اسماعیل سٕندِ اولاد منٛزٕ کِنانہ، کِنانہ سٕندِ اولاد منٛزٕ قُریش، قُریشَن منٛزٕ ہاشِم، تہٕ ہاشِم سٕندِ اولاد منٛزٕ چُھنُن بہٕ۔» [مسلم 2/245؛ ترمذی 2/201]
passages.sourceEnglish: "All? selected Ishmael from the sons of Abraham, Kinana from the sons of Ishmael, Quraish from the sons of Kinana, Hashim from the sons of Quraish and He selected me from the sons of Hashim." [Muslim 2/245; Tirmidhi 2/201]

passages.english: Al-‘Abbas bin ‘Abdul-Muttalib quoted the Messenger of Allah ﷺ as saying:

sourceBlocks.text: Al-‘Abbas bin ‘Abdul-Muttalib quoted the Messenger of All? [pbuh] as saying:

passages.kashmiri: عباس بن عبدالمطلب چھُ رَسولُ اللہ ﷺ سُنٛد یہِ فرمان نَقل کَران:
passages.sourceEnglish: Al-‘Abbas bin ‘Abdul-Muttalib quoted the Messenger of All? [pbuh] as saying:

passages.english: "Allah created mankind and chose me from the best whereof, He chose the tribes and selected me from the best whereof; and He chose families and selected me from the best whereof. I am the very best in person and family." [Tirmidhi 2/201]

sourceBlocks.text: "All? created mankind and chose me from the best whereof, He chose the tribes and selected me from the best whereof; and He chose families and selected me from the best whereof. I am the very best in person and family." [Tirmidhi 2/201]

passages.kashmiri: «اللہ تعالہَن کٔر اِنسان پٲدٕ تہٕ تِمَن ہٕندٮ۪ن بَہتریٖن لوٗکھن منٛزٕ چُھنُن بہٕ۔ تَمہِ چُنۍ قبیلہٕ تہٕ تِمَن ہٕندِس بَہتریٖن قبیلَس منٛزٕ چُھنُن بہٕ۔ تَمہِ چُنۍ خاندان تہٕ تِمَن ہٕندِس بَہتریٖن خاندانَس منٛزٕ چُھنُن بہٕ۔ بہٕ چھُس شَخصی حیثیت تہٕ خاندان دۄشوَے لحاظہٕ بَہتریٖن۔» [ترمذی 2/201]
passages.sourceEnglish: "All? created mankind and chose me from the best whereof, He chose the tribes and selected me from the best whereof; and He chose families and selected me from the best whereof. I am the very best in person and family." [Tirmidhi 2/201]

passages.english: Having increased in number, children of ‘Adnan, in pursuit of pastures and water, spread out over various parts of Arabia.

sourceBlocks.text: Having increased in number, children of ‘Adnan, in pursuit of pastures and water, spread out over various parts of Arabia.

passages.kashmiri: عدنان سٕندِ اولادُک تعداد بَڑنہٕ پَتہٕ پھیٚلۍ تِم آب تہٕ چَراگاہٕچ تَلاشَس منٛز عَرَب کٮ۪ن اَلگ اَلگ حِصّن منٛز۔
passages.sourceEnglish: Having increased in number, children of ‘Adnan, in pursuit of pastures and water, spread out over various parts of Arabia.

passages.english: The tribe of ‘Abdul Qais, together with some septs of Bakr bin Wa’il and Tamim, emigrated to Bahrain where they dwelt.

sourceBlocks.text: The tribe of ‘Abdul Qais, together with some septs of Bakr bin Wa’il and Tamim, emigrated to Bahrain where they dwelt.

passages.kashmiri: عبدُالقَیس قبیلہٕ تہٕ بَکر بن وائل تہٕ تَمیم ہٕندۍ کینہہ بجہ کٔرۍ بحرینَس کُن ہجرت، تہٕ تِم گوٚو تَتیٚتھ آباد۔
passages.sourceEnglish: The tribe of ‘Abdul Qais, together with some septs of Bakr bin Wa’il and Tamim, emigrated to Bahrain where they dwelt.

passages.english: Banu Hanifa bin Sa‘b bin Ali bin Bakr went to settle in Hijr, the capital of Yamama. All the tribes of Bakr bin Wa’il lived in an area of land which included Yamama, Bahrain, Saif Kazima, the sea shore, the outer borders of Iraq, Ablah and Hait.

sourceBlocks.text: Banu Hanifa bin Sa‘b bin Ali bin Bakr went to settle in Hijr, the capital of Yamama. All the tribes of Bakr bin Wa’il lived in an area of land which included Yamama, Bahrain, Saif Kazima, the sea shore, the outer borders of Iraq, Ablah and Hait.

passages.kashmiri: بَنو حَنیفہ بن صَعب بن علی بن بَکر گٔیہِ یَمامہ (Yamama) کِس دارالحکومت حِجرَس (Hijr) منٛز روزنہٕ۔ بَکر بن وائل سٕندۍ سٲری قبیلہٕ روٗدۍ اَتھ علاقَس منٛز، یَتھ منٛز یَمامہ، بحرین، سَیف کاظمہ، سمندرُک بَتھ، عراق کۍ نیبرِم سَرحَدی علاقہٕ، اَبلہ تہٕ ہَیت شٲمِل ٲسۍ۔
passages.sourceEnglish: Banu Hanifa bin Sa‘b bin Ali bin Bakr went to settle in Hijr, the capital of Yamama. All the tribes of Bakr bin Wa’il lived in an area of land which included Yamama, Bahrain, Saif Kazima, the sea shore, the outer borders of Iraq, Ablah and Hait.

passages.english: Most of the tribe of Taghlib lived in the Euphrates area while some of them lived with Bakr.

sourceBlocks.text: Most of the tribe of Taghlib lived in the Euphrates area while some of them lived with Bakr.

passages.kashmiri: تَغلِب قبیلُک زیادہٕ حِصّہٕ روٗد فرات دریاوٕ کِس علاقَس منٛز، حالانٛکہِ تِمَن منٛز کینہہ روٗدۍ بَکر قبیلَس سۭتۍ۔
passages.sourceEnglish: Most of the tribe of Taghlib lived in the Euphrates area while some of them lived with Bakr.

passages.english: Banu Tamim lived in Basra semi-desert.

sourceBlocks.text: Banu Tamim lived in Basra semi-desert.

passages.kashmiri: بَنو تَمیم روٗدۍ بَصرہ (Basra) کِس اَدھ ریگستانی علاقَس منٛز۔
passages.sourceEnglish: Banu Tamim lived in Basra semi-desert.

passages.english: Banu Saleem lived in the vicinity of Madinah on the land stretching from Wadi Al- Qura to Khaibar onwards to the eastern mountains to Harrah.

sourceBlocks.text: Banu Saleem lived in the vicinity of Madinah on the land stretching from Wadi Al- Qura to Khaibar onwards to the eastern mountains to Harrah.

passages.kashmiri: بَنو سُلیم روٗدۍ مدینہ نِش، اَتھ علاقَس منٛز یُس وادی القُریٰ پؠٹھٕ خَیبرَس تام تہٕ تَتہٕ مَشرِقی پہاڑن کُن حَرّہ تام پھیٚلمُت اوس۔
passages.sourceEnglish: Banu Saleem lived in the vicinity of Madinah on the land stretching from Wadi Al- Qura to Khaibar onwards to the eastern mountains to Harrah.

passages.english: Thaqif dwelt in Ta’if and Hawazin east of Makkah near Autas on the road from Makkah to Basra.

sourceBlocks.text: Thaqif dwelt in Ta’if and Hawazin east of Makkah near Autas on the road from Makkah to Basra.

passages.kashmiri: ثَقیٖف روٗدۍ طائِفَس (Ta’if) منٛز، تہٕ ہَوازِن روٗدۍ مکہ ہٕنٛدِ مَشرِقَس کُن اَوطاس نِش، مکہ پؠٹھٕ بَصرہ گژھنہٕ واجنہِ وَتہِ پؠٹھ۔
passages.sourceEnglish: Thaqif dwelt in Ta’if and Hawazin east of Makkah near Autas on the road from Makkah to Basra.

passages.english: Banu Asad lived on the land east of Tayma’ and west of Kufa, while family of Tai’ lived between Banu Asad and Tayma’. They were five-day-walk far from Kufa.

sourceBlocks.text: Banu Asad lived on the land east of Taim?#146; and west of Kufa, while family of Tai’ lived between Banu Asad and Taim?#146;. They were five-day-walk far from Kufa.

passages.kashmiri: بَنو اَسد روٗدۍ تَیماء (Tayma) ہٕنٛدِ مَشرِقَس تہٕ کوفہ ہٕنٛدِ مَغرِبَس کُن۔ طَیّ خاندان روٗد بَنو اَسد تہٕ تَیماء دَرمیان۔ یہِ جایہِ ٲس کوفہ پؠٹھٕ پانٛژن دۄہَن ہُنٛد پَیدَل سفر دُور۔
passages.sourceEnglish: Banu Asad lived on the land east of Taim?#146; and west of Kufa, while family of Tai’ lived between Banu Asad and Taim?#146;. They were five-day-walk far from Kufa.

passages.english: Zubyan inhabited the plot of and between Tayma’ and Hawran.

sourceBlocks.text: Zubyan inhabited the plot of and between Taim?#146; and Hawran.

passages.kashmiri: ذُبیان روٗدۍ تَیماء تہٕ حَوران (Hawran) دَرمیان کِس علاقَس منٛز۔
passages.sourceEnglish: Zubyan inhabited the plot of and between Taim?#146; and Hawran.

passages.english: Some septs of Kinana lived in Tihama, while septs of Quraish dwelt in Makkah and its suburbs. Quraish remained completely disunited until Qusai bin Kilab managed to rally their ranks on honourable terms attaching major prominence to their status and importance. [Muhadrat Tareekh Al-Umam Al-Islamiyah 1/15-16]

passages.kashmiri: کِنانہ سٕندۍ کینہہ بجہ ٲسۍ تہامہَس منٛز روزان، تہٕ قُریشَن ہٕندۍ بجہ ٲسۍ مکہ تہٕ اَمہِ زوٚپٲر کٮ۪ن علاقَن منٛز۔ قُریش روٗدۍ اَکھ اَکِس نِش جُدا، یوت تام قُصَیّ بن کِلابَن تِمَن ہٕنٛزٕ صَفہٕ عزّت وٲلٮ۪ن شَرطَن پؠٹھ اَکس کٔرٕنۍ منٛز کامیٲبی حٲصِل کٔر۔ اَمہِ سۭتۍ بٔڑ تِمَن ہٕنٛز حیثیت تہٕ اہمیت۔ [محاضرات تاریخ الامم الاسلامیۃ 1/15–16]
passages.sourceEnglish: Some septs of Kinana lived in Tihama, while septs of Quraish dwelt in Makkah and its suburbs. Quraish remained completely disunited until Qusai bin Kilab managed to rally their ranks on honourable terms attaching major prominence to their status and importance. [Muhadrat Tareekh Al-Umam Al-Islamiyah 1/15-16]
